scenes.credit: launch film from @msdev's post on X

steps.say: Microsoft's new coding models landed in GitHub Copilot on 17 November.

steps.caption: Code 2 Flash, triaging new issues
steps.say: The headline: 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance, at 40% of the cost.

scenes.headline: MAI Code 2: what the headline is made of
scenes.sub: Rebuilt from the data inside Microsoft's own charts
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Quota. The per benchmark numbers sit inside the chart on Microsoft's model page. I pulled them out.

scenes.title: Four benchmarks, and who ran them

steps.say: Three of the four benchmarks were run by Microsoft, on its own platform, in the Copilot command line tool.

steps.term: Harness: the agent loop around the model
steps.say: That is also the harness the model was trained in with reinforcement learning.
It matters. Opus scores 78.7 on Terminal-Bench there, and 87.64 in another harness and setup.
Only FrontierCode came from outside, and Artificial Analysis does not list MAI Code 2 at all.

scenes.title: Mean pass rate, four benchmarks
scenes.say: Averaged, the numbers reproduce. 63.2 against 64.1 and 65.3. Microsoft even rounded its ratios down.

scenes.title: DeepSWE 1.1: cost is price times tokens

steps.say: Think of cost per task as a rectangle. Its width is the price of a token, its height is how many tokens the agent burns.
MAI Code 2's price is a quarter of Sol's. But on DeepSWE it burned about twice the tokens, so it costs half, not a quarter.

steps.term: Promo: half of list, until 17 May 2027
steps.say: That price is a launch promotion. On 17 May 2027 it doubles, and the two rectangles are the same size.
Now divide by the pass rate, since failures are billed too. At list price, MAI Code 2 is the dearer one per resolved task.

left.title: Until 17 May 2027
items: Half of Luna's price per token
left.say: Flash is half of GPT-6 Luna's price for now, and 65% of its cost per task.

right.title: From 17 May 2027
right.say: Then its price becomes Luna's, token for token, and it costs 130% of Luna per task. It still passes more tasks.

steps.say: The model card disagrees with itself. Its autonomy table puts MAI Code 2 at 60.2 on DeepSWE.

steps.caption: The headline table says 73.2
steps.say: The headline table says 73.2, and nothing explains the gap.

scenes.title: Terminal-Bench 4, the hard one
scenes.note: different harnesses: a direction, not a gap
scenes.say: On the hardest terminal benchmark, MAI Code 2 sits below Haiku. Microsoft says long horizon work is out of scope, and it shows.

scenes.credit: launch film from @msdev's post on X

steps.say: It is in Copilot today. Flash is on every plan, and in Foundry as a preview.

steps.caption: 1.05M tokens of context, both models
steps.say: No weights, and no outside benchmark yet.

scenes.text: Honest arithmetic on Microsoft's own harness. Half the discount is price, and the price doubles on 17 May 2027.
scenes.say: The arithmetic is honest, on Microsoft's own harness. Half the discount is the price, and the price doubles in May.

recap: Three of four benchmarks run by Microsoft
Flash costs more than Luna after May
scenes.say: Microsoft's harness, price times tokens, and a promotion with an end date. Thanks for watching!
